title: DB: Create households, household_members, household_invites tables
description:
Create Supabase migration with three new tables:

**households:** id (uuid PK), name (text NOT NULL, default 'My Kitchen'), created_by (uuid FK auth.users ON DELETE SET NULL), created_at, updated_at. RLS: members can view, owner can update/delete.

**household_members:** id (uuid PK), household_id (uuid FK households ON DELETE CASCADE), user_id (uuid FK auth.users ON DELETE CASCADE), role (text NOT NULL CHECK IN ('owner','member')), joined_at (timestamptz default now()). UNIQUE(household_id, user_id). RLS: members of same household can view, owner can insert/delete.

**household_invites:** id (uuid PK), household_id (uuid FK households ON DELETE CASCADE), invited_by (uuid FK auth.users), email (text NOT NULL), token (text UNIQUE NOT NULL default gen_random_uuid()), status (text NOT NULL default 'pending' CHECK IN ('pending','accepted','expired')), created_at (timestamptz default now()), expires_at (timestamptz default now() + interval '7 days'). RLS: household members can view, members can insert, token-holder can update status to accepted.

Files: supabase/migrations/new migration file
Acceptance: Tables created with proper indexes, FKs, and RLS policies.
close_reason: Migration files created

title: DB: Add household_id to content tables and migrate existing data
description:
Add household_id (uuid FK households) to: recipes, recipe_groups, grocery_lists, pantry_items.

Migration steps:
1. Add household_id column as NULLABLE to each table
2. For each existing user: create a household, add user as owner in household_members
3. Backfill: UPDATE each table SET household_id = (SELECT household_id FROM household_members WHERE user_id = table.user_id LIMIT 1)
4. ALTER each column to NOT NULL
5. Add indexes on household_id for each table

Files: supabase/migrations/new migration file
Acceptance: All existing data has household_id set. Column is NOT NULL. Indexes created.
close_reason: Migration files created

title: DB: Update all RLS policies to household membership check
description:
Drop and recreate RLS policies on all content tables to check household membership instead of direct user_id.

New pattern for recipes, recipe_groups, grocery_lists, pantry_items:
- SELECT: household_id IN (SELECT household_id FROM household_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
- INSERT: same check on WITH CHECK, plus user_id = auth.uid() for attribution
- UPDATE: same membership check
- DELETE: same membership check

Child tables (grocery_items, recipe_group_items) keep their existing pattern (inherit through parent FK), but the parent's RLS now checks household membership.

Files: supabase/migrations/new migration file
Acceptance: Any household member can CRUD all content in their household. Non-members cannot access. Verify with test queries.
close_reason: Migration files created
